advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Harden validate-gerrit-repair-refspecs.sh to also reject refspecs whose destination is a short/unqualified name that git resolves under refs/heads/ (e.g. any dest not starting with refs/recovery/), not just literal refs/heads[/*].
evidence: infra/scripts/validate-gerrit-repair-refspecs.sh:14: `*:refs/heads | *:refs/heads/*)`
Git fetch treats an unqualified RHS (no `refs/` prefix) as under `refs/heads/`; `refs/heads/main:main` therefore lands in `refs/heads/main` but matches neither case pattern
Ticket AC c8dc-9fb2-ddfa-45d0: 'The guard hard-rejects any refspec whose destination is refs/heads/*' -- a short-name destination that git resolves to refs/heads/* is not rejected
advisory.finding: The refspec guard only rejects destinations spelled 'refs/heads' or 'refs/heads/*', but git fetch expands an unqualified destination to refs/heads/<name>. A refspec like 'refs/heads/main:main' writes directly to the live branch refs/heads/main yet passes the guard (exit 0), so the exact failure class the guard was written to block can bypass it.
scenarios: Operator writes a fetch refspec with a short destination name (e.g. `refs/heads/main:main` or `refs/heads/main:foo`) which git places under refs/heads/, moving a live branch
advisory.suggested_fix: Reject any refspec whose destination is not explicitly under the allowed quarantine namespace: e.g. after stripping the leading '+', split on ':' and require the RHS to match refs/recovery/github/*; treat a missing colon or an unqualified RHS as a rejection rather than allowing it.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Convert the guard to an allowlist (require destination under refs/recovery/github/*) so unanticipated destination forms are rejected rather than silently permitted.
evidence: infra/scripts/validate-gerrit-repair-refspecs.sh:10-19: bad defaults to 0 and only flips on the two explicit patterns; the `case` has no catch-all reject/allowlist arm
infra/scripts/validate-gerrit-repair-refspecs.sh:21: `exit "$bad"` returns success for every unmatched form
advisory.finding: The guard's allow-path is a default-permit: any refspec that does not match the two reject patterns is accepted, so unrecognized/malformed destinations (short names, HEAD, refs/tags/*, empty RHS) silently pass. The oracle cannot distinguish 'checked and safe' from 'destination form not anticipated by the case arms'.
scenarios: A repair refspec targeting any destination other than the two literal patterns is treated as safe by omission

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct runbook step 8 to invoke the mirror guard as `python -m rebar.mirror_guard` (matching the registered entrypoint), not the nonexistent `rebar mirror-guard` subcommand.
evidence: infra/runbooks/gerrit-object-store-repair.md:77: `rebar mirror-guard --replication --merged-reachability 50`
pyproject.toml:326: `rebar = "rebar.cli:main"` and pyproject.toml:327 `rebar-mcp = "rebar.mcp_server:main"` are the only [project.scripts]; no `mirror-guard` script

src/rebar/mirror_guard.py:397: `argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="rebar.mirror_guard", ...)` — the module is invoked as a module, and .github/workflows/mirror-guard.yml:57 runs `python -m rebar.mirror_guard --replication --merged-reachability`
Bounded search of src/rebar/_cli for `mirror` returns no subcommand registration
infra/runbooks/gerrit-object-store-repair.md:77: `... --merged-reachability 50`
src/rebar/mirror_guard.py:404-408: `--merged-reachability` is defined with `action="store_true"` (takes no value)
src/rebar/mirror_guard.py:426-431: `--merged-limit` (type=int, default=100) is the option that sets `number of recent merged Gerrit changes to check for branch reachability`
advisory.finding: The runbook step 8 invokes `rebar mirror-guard`, but there is no `mirror-guard` subcommand on the `rebar` CLI. The only console scripts are `rebar` and `rebar-mcp`, and the mirror-guard module is invoked as `python -m rebar.mirror_guard` elsewhere. The documented operator command does not exist and will fail.
merged_from: The runbook step 8 passes `50` to `--merged-reachability`, but that option is a boolean flag (action='store_true'). The count of recent merged changes to check is the separate `--merged-limit` option. As documented, the command passes an unexpected argument and does not set the intended limit.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that invokes the guard with no arguments and asserts exit code 2 plus the usage message on stderr.
evidence: validate-gerrit-repair-refspecs.sh lines 5-8: `if [ "$#" -eq 0 ]; then echo "usage: ..." >&2; exit 2; fi`
Added tests only cover a single bad refspec and a single good refspec; no test invokes the script with no arguments to assert `returncode == 2` and the usage text.
Named violating input: `bash validate-gerrit-repair-refspecs.sh` (no args).
validate-gerrit-repair-refspecs.sh lines 11-19 iterate `for raw in "$@"` and set `bad=1` on any match, exiting `"$bad"`.
Both added guard tests pass exactly one refspec; no test passes multiple refspecs where a later one is the offending destination.
Named violating input: `bash validate-gerrit-repair-refspecs.sh refs/heads/main:refs/recovery/github/main refs/heads/dev:refs/heads/dev` (second refspec bad) must still exit non-zero.
validate-gerrit-repair-refspecs.sh line 12: `refspec="${raw#+}"` then `case "$refspec" in *:refs/heads/*)`

The `+` prefix appears on the source side of the tested refspec; the destination `refs/heads/*` matches the glob regardless of the `+`, so the strip on the destination is not what makes the test pass.
Named input distinguishing the strip: a destination-side leading '+' such as `refs/heads/main:+refs/heads/main` is never tested.
advisory.finding: The new guard script's empty-argument path (usage message + exit 2) is newly added behavior that is not tested; a named violating input is invoking the script with zero arguments, which should print the usage string and exit 2.
merged_from: The guard's multi-refspec loop that rejects when ANY of several refspecs is bad (lines 11-19) is newly added but only ever tested with a single refspec; a mixed batch (one good + one bad refspec) is untested, so a regression that stopped scanning after the first argument would not be caught.

The reject test does not exercise the newly-added leading-'+' stripping (line 12): the chosen input `+refs/heads/*:refs/heads/*` matches the `*:refs/heads/*` case pattern whether or not the `+` is stripped, so removing the `refspec="${raw#+}"` line would not fail this test.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test calling the script with an empty argv, asserting `result.returncode == 2` and `"usage:" in result.stderr`.
